Cholera Outbreak Disrupts Saudi Chemicals Industry, Hits Saudi Basic Industries Corp Operations

RIYADH, June 12 – A cholera outbreak among workers has disrupted operations at several chemicals plants in Saudi Arabia, leading to reduced output and concerns over supply chain stability, industry officials said Wednesday.

Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), one of the country’s largest chemicals producers, confirmed that it has temporarily cut capacity at its Jubail and Yanbu sites, as dozens of employees have been hospitalized or placed in isolation following positive diagnoses.

“SABIC places the highest priority on the health and safety of its employees. We are working closely with health authorities to contain the outbreak and ensure affected workers receive the necessary care,” the company said in a statement. The company declined to specify the exact number of cases or the scale of production cuts.

At least two other major chemical producers, including the locally headquartered Al-Maha Petrochemicals, have reported disruptions, according to the Saudi Chemicals Industry Association. “We estimate that overall output across the industry has dropped by 15% since the outbreak began last week,” said association spokesperson Fahd Al-Qahtani.

Local health authorities in the Eastern Province have deployed emergency medical teams and launched disinfection protocols at several industrial sites. “Our immediate focus is on preventing further transmission among workers and their families,” said Dr. Laila Al-Dosari, a regional health official.

Analysts warned that if the outbreak is not contained quickly, shipments of key chemical products could face delays. “The chemicals sector is a backbone of Saudi manufacturing, and prolonged disruptions could have broader implications for downstream supply chains,” said Riyadh-based industry analyst Khaled Mansour.

The outbreak is ongoing and authorities have not announced when normal operations might resume.
